attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his signed prediction post. He endorses it as a prediction for 2026.

semantics.note: The unhedged 'will' makes this a scored forecast. Reading 'the midterms' as the 2026 US midterms fits the context. The novelty element ('first time') is kept. The nearby 'may' sentence about Trump is a separate statement and is correctly left out.

contract.note: This is a plain-reading contract. Reading 'election issue' as a salient campaign and voter issue, and 'first time' as compared with earlier national cycles, is an ordinary and fair reading. The result depends on these interpretations, since the speaker gave no threshold.

evidence.note: Pew poll fielded Sept 28–Oct 4, 2026, before the cutoff: 44% of voters rate AI very important. This supports voter interest in 2026 but says nothing about novelty.
AdImpact measured data-center ads in August 2026. The ads are not separated into AI-specific messaging, and the data-center issue ranks 43rd of 78. Context only.
Roll Call, Sept 2026: Warner ran an ad on AI. The article also says AI-risk ads were rare, so this is only partial support for 2026 salience.
A 2019 Yang interview shows AI and automation were raised in an earlier cycle. It does not show comparable salience across that cycle, so it neither settles nor refutes 'first time'.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is Nov 3, 2026, after the Oct 28 evaluation date. Early resolution needs both 2026 salience and a substantive historical comparison showing novelty. Pew and Roll Call show some 2026 voter interest and campaign messaging. No admitted evidence gives a cycle-wide historical comparison, and the Yang example does not show comparable earlier salience. The early-resolution rule is not met, so the forecast is not scored yet.
